items.title: How GGLink hosts its apps
items.body: GGLink's apps run on a shared Apache VPS (the "gglink server") behind Cloudflare. The server runs mod_php 7.4 globally for its older PHP sites; GGMoney needs PHP 8.1, so it alone runs through PHP 8.1 FPM, set per virtual host with a SetHandler to the php8.1-fpm socket, and it uses MySQL 8, which was already installed. Node apps run as pm2 processes bound to 127.0.0.1 and are reached through Apache as a reverse proxy: GGSocial's web process is ggsocial-web (next start on port 3200) with a ggsocial-scheduler process that ticks its cron endpoints (publishing every 60 seconds); GGLearn is gglearn-web on 127.0.0.1:3400. GGSocial's database is PostgreSQL 16 in Docker, bound to localhost with a named volume; GGLearn uses a SQLite file (data/gglearn.db). pm2 survives reboots because the pm2-root service is enabled and the process list is saved. Public addresses follow the pattern <app>.gglink.co.uk (gglearn, ggsocial, ggmoney). Source: gglearn/README.md and deploy/, ggsocial/DEPLOY.md and ecosystem.config.cjs, ggmoney/DEPLOY.md.

items.title: Apache, TLS and Cloudflare
items.body: TLS certificates come from Let's Encrypt via certbot and renew automatically (a certbot timer and the webroot method); nobody renews them by hand. Cloudflare's SSL mode matters: GGMoney must be set to Full (strict), because HMRC OAuth tokens travel on the Cloudflare-to-origin hop and Flexible mode would send them in the clear. GGMoney's vhosts set AllowOverride All, which is not optional: every security rule lives in .htaccess, and without it source and config are downloadable. GGLearn's app is reachable only through Cloudflare: deploy/apache-cloudflare-only.conf allows Cloudflare's published IP ranges plus localhost, so the client address the app derives from X-Forwarded-For cannot be spoofed by bypassing Cloudflare. It is pulled in with a plain Include, not IncludeOptional, so if the file is missing Apache refuses to load the config instead of silently serving the site to everyone. deploy/update-cloudflare-ips.sh regenerates it from Cloudflare's published ranges, and refuses to write a list that looks wrong, so a bad fetch can never produce an empty (lock-everyone-out) allow-list; afterwards you review the diff, commit, deploy and reload Apache. certbot copies the :80 vhost into the :443 one, so the copy must carry the same Include line. For GGSocial the live :443 vhost is a regular file in /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/ (not a symlink) and has drifted from sites-available; editing the sites-available copy passes apachectl configtest, reloads cleanly and changes nothing. Edit the sites-enabled copy, check which file each vhost comes from with apachectl -S, back it up first, then apachectl configtest && systemctl reload apache2. Source: ggmoney/DEPLOY.md, gglearn/deploy/, ggsocial/DEPLOY.md.

items.title: Deploying a Node app (GGLearn)
items.body: GGLearn deploys on every push to main through GitHub Actions, which runs deploy/deploy.sh over SSH (it uses the host alias gglink-live). The script rsyncs the repo to /var/www/gglearn.gglink.co.uk excluding node_modules, .next, .git, data/*.db* and .env*, so the production database and secrets are never overwritten. The server's login shell is fish, which cannot parse bash grouping or &&/|| chains, so the remote steps are piped into bash. A flock on /tmp/gglearn-deploy.lock stops two deploys running at once. The remote steps are npm ci, npx drizzle-kit push, npm run build, pm2 startOrRestart ecosystem.config.cjs and pm2 save. There is deliberately no --force on drizzle-kit push: when a schema change would delete rows (for example a NOT NULL column added to a table that has data) it must stop and fail the deploy instead of running a delete. Finally the script polls http://127.0.0.1:3400/ up to ten times, three seconds apart, and fails the deploy unless it gets HTTP 200, printing the last pm2 error logs. The server uses Node 20, so Node 21+ APIs must be avoided, and better-sqlite3 is kept on a version with a Linux Node 20 prebuild. Source: gglearn/deploy/deploy.sh and README.md.

questions.prompt: You need to host a new small Node app at newapp.gglink.co.uk on the existing server. Describe the steps and settings, following how GGLearn and GGSocial are hosted.
questions.answer: Create an Apache vhost for newapp.gglink.co.uk that reverse-proxies to the app on 127.0.0.1 and a chosen free port (the app listens only on localhost); get a Let's Encrypt certificate with certbot (renews automatically) and check the :443 copy carries any Include lines; keep Cloudflare in front, set to Full (strict), and consider the Cloudflare-only allow-list used for GGLearn; run the app under pm2 with an ecosystem file, enable pm2 startup and pm2 save; keep secrets in a .env on the server with chmod 600 and exclude .env and the database from rsync; deploy with a script that uses a lock, npm ci, a schema push without --force, a build, pm2 startOrRestart and a health check that fails the deploy unless the app returns 200; run configtest before reloading Apache; and arrange backups of the database and any uploads, since nothing is scheduled by default.
questions.rubric: A good answer includes most of: Apache vhost with reverse proxy to 127.0.0.1:PORT; certbot/Let's Encrypt; Cloudflare Full (strict) and optionally the Cloudflare-only allow-list; pm2 with startup and save; .env on the server (chmod 600) excluded from rsync; deploy script with flock, npm ci, schema push without --force, build, pm2 restart and a health check; apachectl configtest before reload; backups of database and uploads. Credit each correct element; mark down anything that exposes the app on a public port, overwrites .env or the database, or skips backups.

items.title: Traps learned the hard way (GGSocial)
items.body: GGSocial's deploy notes record several traps. rsync --delete destroys production secrets: .env exists only on the server, so without --exclude .env rsync deletes it as not in source (and .env.local, a symlink to it, goes too). Losing APP_SECRET logs everyone out and makes stored platform tokens undecryptable, so channels must be reconnected; copies of .env live in /root/ggsocial-backups/env-*. npm ci silently skips the Linux Tailwind binary because the lockfile is generated on macOS, so the build dies with a missing module; the deploy pins it with an explicit npm install --no-save at the same version as @tailwindcss/oxide, keeping it out of the committed lockfile. Turbopack caches a failed build, so the deploy builds into a fresh .next-new and swaps it in, which also keeps the old build serving until the new one is ready. A login shell sources nvm and puts an old Node first, so Next 16 refuses to build (it needs Node >= 20.9.0) while pm2 runs /usr/bin/node; the script puts /usr/bin first so install, build and runtime agree. A failed build that happens after rm -rf .next leaves a running server without a build directory, so check /login immediately. The login shell is fish: anything with $(...) passed straight to ssh fails to parse (the backup step once silently produced no backup), so the server half is streamed over stdin with bash -s. The schema is pushed without --force, with < /dev/null so a stop fails fast instead of hanging on a prompt. A browser tab left open across a deploy holds the old build's Server Action ids; deploymentId and a pinned NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY in .env fix it. Source: ggsocial/DEPLOY.md.

questions.prompt: A GGSocial deploy fails during the build, part-way through. List what you check and do immediately, and what the deploy script does to limit the damage.
questions.answer: Check immediately that the site still answers: curl http://127.0.0.1:3200/login should return 200 and pm2 list should show both processes running. The script builds into a fresh .next-new and only swaps it in on success, so the old build should still be serving, but a build that fails after rm -rf .next would leave no build directory, so verify at once. Read the build error: common causes are the missing Linux Tailwind binary (the script pins it with npm install --no-save), the wrong Node on the PATH (Next needs 20.9 or newer, and the script puts /usr/bin first), or a cached failed build (Turbopack caches failures, hence the fresh directory). Confirm the database backup in /root/ggsocial-backups was taken before the schema push, and do not use --force on drizzle-kit push. Fix the cause, then redeploy.
questions.rubric: A good answer: checks the site and pm2 first; knows the build goes into .next-new and is swapped on success; names plausible causes (Tailwind binary, Node version, cached failure); mentions the pre-deploy database backup and that schema push has no --force; reads logs before changing anything; redeploys after fixing. Partial credit for generic troubleshooting; no credit for suggestions that delete .env or force a schema push.

questions.prompt: A colleague ran `rsync -az --delete ./ server:/var/www/ggsocial.gglink.co.uk/` without any excludes and now GGSocial will not start. What happened, how do you recover, and how do you prevent it happening again?
questions.answer: rsync --delete removed files that are not in the source. .env lives only on the server, so it was deleted (and .env.local, a symlink to it, went too), along with anything else not in the repo such as uploads under .data. Recover .env from the copies in /root/ggsocial-backups/env-* (and note /root/.ggsocial holds only the basic-auth, cron and pg secrets, not the full file), restore uploads from the backup, check APP_SECRET and NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY are intact (a lost APP_SECRET logs everyone out and makes stored platform tokens undecryptable), restart pm2 and confirm /login returns 200. Prevent it by always using the deploy script (npm run deploy), which excludes .env and syncs directories, and by keeping .env and uploads backed up on a schedule.
questions.rubric: A good answer: explains that --delete removes server-only files such as .env (and symlinked .env.local) and possibly uploads; recovers .env from /root/ggsocial-backups/env-* and uploads from backup; notes the consequence of losing APP_SECRET; restarts and checks /login; and prevents recurrence by using the deploy script with its excludes and by scheduling backups. Partial credit for naming the cause without a recovery plan.

items.title: Secrets, backups and consistent copies
items.body: Production secrets live in a .env on the server (chmod 600) and never in the repo. GGSocial's basic-auth file is /etc/apache2/ggsocial.htpasswd owned root:www-data with mode 640. GGSocial uploads are on local disk (.data/uploads), so they must be backed up. Its documented database backup is a manual command: docker exec ggsocial-pg pg_dump -U ggsocial ggsocial | gzip > ggsocial-$(date +%F).sql.gz plus a copy of .data/uploads, and the notes say nothing is scheduled, so it is worth adding to whatever already backs up the other sites. The deploy script also takes a database backup into /root/ggsocial-backups/ before changing anything. GGLearn's SQLite database runs in WAL mode, so copying the .db file alone would miss recent writes; deploy/seed-content.sh takes a consistent snapshot with better-sqlite3's backup, rehearses with DRY=1 against a copy so the live database is untouched, and otherwise takes a consistent backup before running the content steps in order (curriculum, AI tracks, knowledge, structure, careers, customer content). GGMoney's config.local.php (database credentials, HMRC settings) is on the server only and is never uploaded; its deploy script never uploads storage/ either. Source: ggsocial/DEPLOY.md, gglearn/deploy/seed-content.sh, ggmoney/DEPLOY.md.

items.title: GGMoney: sandbox, HMRC and safe deploys
items.body: GGMoney is deployed at ggmoney.gglink.co.uk and is in sandbox mode: APP_ENV stays sandbox until production credentials exist and a parallel run has been done. APP_DEBUG must be false in production, always, because true prints stack traces to the browser. APP_URL must be HTTPS because HMRC requires it. While testing, MAIL_REDIRECT sends every email to a chosen address instead of the real recipient. The HMRC redirect URI is https://ggmoney.gglink.co.uk/settings/hmrc/callback, character for character. When connecting HMRC, sign in with the Government Gateway account for that company: the token binds to whichever VAT enrolment sits behind the account, so the wrong company's login will happily file against the wrong VRN; do this once per company. The first-run /setup page creates the first user and both companies with a standard chart of accounts, then disappears for good. The deploy script (bin/deploy.sh, with --dry-run) refuses to upload anything if a file fails to parse or a test fails, syncs, fixes ownership, applies migrations and runs deploy-check.php; deploy-check.php only reports and refuses to run over plain HTTP. There are no Composer dependencies. Source: ggmoney/DEPLOY.md.

items.title: Health checks, logs and what is open on purpose
items.body: To check GGSocial without redeploying: curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3200/login should return 200, and pm2 list --no-color shows the processes. Logs are pm2 logs ggsocial-web and ggsocial-scheduler, and /var/log/apache2/ggsocial.gglink.co.uk-error.log; GGLearn's Apache logs are gglearn-error.log and gglearn-access.log in the Apache log directory, and pm2 logs gglearn-web shows the app. The database shell is docker exec -it ggsocial-pg psql -U ggsocial -d ggsocial. The GGSocial scheduler always logs one 'tick failed: fetch failed' during a restart, which is expected; repeated ones are not. Two GGSocial routes are deliberately let past its basic-auth wall in both vhosts: /api/agent/ (agents send an X-Agent-Token header because basic auth already uses Authorization; every route there rejects requests without a valid, unrevoked token) and /api/media/file/ (Instagram, Facebook, Pinterest and TikTok fetch post media with no credentials, so uploaded files are readable by anyone with the unguessable URL; if that is not acceptable for a client's unreleased content, move media to S3 with MEDIA_DRIVER=s3 and keep the app behind basic auth). Short links under /l/ are also let through. Changing APP_SECRET logs everyone out. Source: ggsocial/DEPLOY.md and gglearn/deploy/.

questions.prompt: Which command lists the processes pm2 is running?
How do you check that GGSocial answers locally after a deploy?

options.text: Run npm test on the server

questions.prompt: Where do you read GGSocial's web process logs?
questions.hint: The scheduler has its own: pm2 logs ggsocial-scheduler.

questions.prompt: How do you open a database shell for GGSocial?

options.text: docker exec -it ggsocial-pg psql -U ggsocial -d ggsocial

questions.prompt: The GGSocial scheduler logs one 'tick failed: fetch failed' after a restart. What does it mean?

options.text: Expected during the restart window; repeated ones are not

questions.prompt: Where are GGLearn's Apache logs?

options.text: gglearn-error.log and gglearn-access.log in the Apache log directory

questions.hint: ErrorLog and CustomLog in its vhost.

questions.prompt: After a deploy the app returns an error. Which two quick checks come first?

options.text: pm2 error logs and a local curl to the app's port

questions.hint: See what is failing before changing anything.

questions.prompt: Why is /api/agent/ let through GGSocial's basic-auth wall?

options.text: Because basic auth is broken for APIs
Agents authenticate with an X-Agent-Token header (basic auth already uses Authorization), and every route there rejects requests without a valid, unrevoked token

questions.prompt: Why is /api/media/file/ open, and what is the catch?

options.text: It is open only to Cloudflare
Platforms such as Instagram and Facebook fetch media without credentials, so anyone with the unguessable URL can read it

questions.hint: For unreleased client content consider S3 with MEDIA_DRIVER=s3.

questions.prompt: A client has unreleased content in GGSocial and open media URLs are not acceptable. What do the notes suggest?

options.text: Move media to S3 with MEDIA_DRIVER=s3 and keep the app itself behind basic auth
